Park and Recreation Commission

  Inglewood, California
  June 4, 2026

The Inglewood Park and Recreation Commission meeting was convened in the Council
Chambers located on the ninth floor of City Hall on June 4, 2026. Commissioner Denmon
called the meeting to order at 6:00 p.m. followed by the flag salute.

Ashley Ferrette announced the presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Commissioner Lee Denmon - District 1, Commissioner Alex Monge -
  District 3, Commissioner Henry Brown - Commissioner at Large
  Absent:  District 2 - Vacant, District 4 - Vacant

City Personnel present for the meeting were as follows:

  Thomas Uwal  Director of Parks, Recreation and Community Services
  Sylvia Olmedo  Recreation Supervisor
  Baz Devlia  Human Services Superintendent
  Brian McClure  Parks Administration Superintendent
  Ashley Ferrette  Staff Assistant

PUBLIC COMMENTS. None.

MINUTES. May minutes tabled to the next Commission meeting.

DIRECTOR’S BUSINESS.

REPORT - PARKS. Parks Administration Superintendent Brian McClure reported the following:
Parks Division - Next week, Inglewood will host the FIFA World Cup. Our crews have been busy
preparing the City by enhancing landscape areas, cleaning public spaces, and installing new plant
material in medians throughout the community. May 30th, the City partnered with Clean California
to host a park cleanup event at Edward Vincent Park. Approximately 40 volunteers participated,
including members of the Alpha Kappa Alpha Sorority, helping to beautify the park and surrounding
areas. Tree Division - City tree crews are currently removing trees identified by our tree
maintenance contractor, West Coast Arborists (WCA), doing routine ficus and elm pruning
operations. WCA crews continue ficus and elm pruning activities in Districts 1 and 2. In addition,
palm tree trimming operations began on June 1 and are ongoing throughout the City. Graffiti
Division - Graffiti removal staff have been actively responding to vandalism incidents throughout
the City. District 4 has experienced a significant increase in graffiti activity, with repeated tagging
incidents occurring along Crenshaw Boulevard between Century Boulevard and Imperial Highway.
Edward Vincent Park has also been repeatedly targeted by vandals, requiring ongoing graffiti
removal efforts throughout the park grounds.

  1
   Park and Recreation Commission

REPORT - RECREATION. Recreation Supervisor Sylvia Olmedo reported the following: Early
Learners Program – This year’s theme for the Early Learners Summer Program is Wild West, where
the focus is on ongoing development of key early learning. We are offering half day programing at
Rogers Park for ages 3 – 5, where they’ll attend three (3) days out of the week; Monday,
Wednesday, and Friday from 9:00 a.m. to 12:00 p.m. The program will operate from June 15th to
July 24th We have a full day Kiddie Camp at Siminski Park, operating Monday through Friday from
9:00 a.m. to 4:00p.m. Summer Day Camp - We are pleased to report that all of our summer camp
programs have reached full enrollment. We are excited to provide enriching, engaging, and
memorable experiences for hundreds of campers this summer. Summer Day Camp programs will
be offered at Rogers Park and Darby Park from June 15 through August 7, featuring a variety of
recreational activities, educational opportunities, special events, and field trips designed to
promote learning, friendship, and fun in a safe and supportive environment. Swimming Pool - The
Edward Vincent Jr. Park swimming pool will experience a delayed opening this year. It was
originally scheduled to open on June 15, but the main pool pump and motor are inoperable. We
are working with a vendor to resolve the issue as quickly as possible. A short-form agreement for
the necessary repairs is being processed, and we are hopeful the work can be completed within
the next three (3) weeks to minimize impacts on our summer aquatics programs. Movies in the
Park - Our first Movies in the Park event will take place on Saturday, June 27, at Edward Vincent
Park. The featured film will be Disney's Hoppers. Pre-movie activities will begin at 6:00 p.m., and
the movie will start at dusk. Everyone has already received a copy of the Movies in the Park flyer,
which includes additional details on dates, locations, and event times.

REPORT - HUMAN SERVICES. Human Services Superintendent Baz Devlia reported on the
following: Senior Transportation - The City of Inglewood’s paratransit program continues to
provide trips to seniors and the disabled community in Inglewood and Hawthorne. Bus operators
are participating in online driver training. This time around, the topic is distracted driving. All bus
operators will be completing a refresher training on distracted driving as well as having attended
a refresher training on how to properly pre-trip their vehicles. On the service end, seniors have
enjoyed being transported to Edward Vincent Jr. Park to participate in free tennis lessons which
came to a close on May 28th seniors found tennis to be great for socializing, getting outdoors and
exercising. Elderly Nutrition Program - The Senior Center proudly serves approximately 460
seniors each week through both home-delivered meals for homebound individuals and congregate
dining services. To further support our community's nutritional needs, monthly shelf-stable meal
boxes are distributed in collaboration with the Los Angeles Food Bank. Senior Center Activities -
On June 11, we will be showing the movie “Curveball” at 1:30 p.m. On June 12, The Alzheimer’s
Association will conduct a presentation on “10 Healthy Habits for Your Brain” from 10:00 a.m. –
11:00 a.m. On June 15, LA County of Mental Health will be conducting a presentation on “How
Much is Too Much” from 10:45 a.m. – 11:45 a.m. On June 17, Special Father’s Day celebration,
poetry reading, a gift, special performance by the Inspirational Choir From 10:00 a.m. – 11:00 a.m.
On June 19, we will have a special Juneteenth Program from 10:00 a.m. – 11:00 a.m. with a fashion
show by our Arts of Design, poetry, and special performances by the Inspirational Choir, and
Saxophone performance by Aro our senior. On June 25, we will be celebrating quarterly birthdays
(April, May, June) from 2:00 p.m. – 4:00 p.m.

  2
   Park and Recreation Commission

REPORT - DIRECTOR. Parks, Recreation and Community Services Department Director Thomas
Uwal reported on the following: The City of Inglewood is excited to present The Wood Cup
Community Event - a free public watch party for the FIFA World Cup 2026 USA vs. Paraguay match
will take place on June 12, 2026, accompanied by a vibrant street festival celebrating soccer,
culture, and community spirit. From 2:00 p.m. to 6:00 p.m., nearly one mile of Market Street will
be transformed into a vehicle-free festival zone featuring family-friendly entertainment,
interactive games, turf soccer activities, food vendors, and community engagement opportunities
for all ages. The event is funded through a Metro Open Streets Grant, with convenient access
provided by the Metro K Line, which stops directly at the Market Street festival area. As the world
turns its attention to the FIFA World Cup, The Wood Cup offers residents and visitors an
opportunity to experience the culture, creativity, and energy of the City of Inglewood. The USA vs.
Paraguay match at SoFi Stadium begins at 6:00 p.m. and this free community celebration provides
an exciting and affordable alternative for fans who may not attend the match in person. Little
League Relocation from Rogers Park to Darby Park - The Inglewood Little League program will
temporarily relocate from Rogers Park to Darby Park beginning September 7, 2026, due to
construction improvements at Rogers Park. The project is expected to last approximately six (6)
months before the league returns to Rogers Park. Both baseball fields at Darby Park will be
available for Little League activities, allowing the organization to plan accordingly as registration
for the upcoming season opens. Scheduled practice days will be Tuesdays, Wednesdays, and
Thursdays from 5:30 p.m. to 8:30 p.m., with games taking place on Saturdays and Sundays from
9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Inglewood Independence Music Festival - The annual Inglewood
Independence Music Festival will return to Darby Park on July 4, 2026, for a day of celebration and
entertainment for the entire community. This free, family-friendly event will feature live
performances across a variety of musical genres, including R&B, Latin, Jazz, and Hip-Hop, along
with food trucks, local vendors, and community activities. The City looks forward to welcoming
residents and visitors for another memorable Independence Day celebration. Family Unity Day at
Darby Park - The City of Inglewood’s annual Family Unity Day, hosted by Councilwoman Gloria D.
Gray, will take place on Saturday, August 1, 2026, at Darby Park. This community event celebrates
family, culture, music, food, health, and togetherness. Family Unity Day is an opportunity for
residents to come together, strengthen community connections, and enjoy a day of fellowship and
celebration. The City looks forward to another successful and uplifting event for the entire
community.

PUBLIC COMMENTS. Bernice Brown thanked the department for all that they do.

COMMISSIONER COMMENTS. Commissioner Denmon welcomed Alex Monge, the newest
Commissioner representing District 3. Commissioner Brown noted that this year’s Annual
Memorial Day Service was not well attended possibly be due to back to back events being held. He
suggested spreading out future events and dates. He also made mention spearheading an event to
bring men of the community together.

There being no further business to be presented, Commissioner Denmon declared the meeting
adjourned at the hour of 6:28 p.m.
